## Overview

As an experimental computer scientist, the goal of my research is to design,
implement, and evaluate techniques and tools that support the creation of
useful, dependable, and efficient software. My research addresses the challenges
in fields such as software engineering, software testing, and computer systems.
I conduct this research with undergraduates at [Allegheny
College](http://www.allegheny.edu), graduate students and professors at several
universities (e.g., University of Sheffield and the University of Passau), and
colleagues in industry. Keep reading for more details!

## Details

My research is empirical because it involves the application of the scientific
method to formulate problem statements, carry out experiments, take
observations, statistically analyze and visualize the data sets, and draw
conclusions based on the results. Each research project focuses on the
development, evaluation, and maintenance of [software](/software/) artifacts
that can be used in both empirical studies and real-world practice by
undergraduate and graduate students, software engineers, data scientists, and
computer scientists in both academia and industry.

In addition to supporting my professional [service](/service/), my research
results in award-winning and frequently cited research
[papers](/research/papers/), oft-complimented
[presentations](/research/presentations/), and useful free and open-source
[software](/software/). I also leverage my research expertise as a co-host of
[Software Engineering Radio](https://se-radio.net/), the podcast for which I
conduct [interviews](https://se-radio.net/team/gregory-kapfhammer/) with the
world's leading experts on topics like automated refactoring and property-based
testing. My research focuses on software engineering and software testing,
examples of which are described in these summaries that reference key papers.
Please click the {{< iconify fa6-solid book-open >}} icon next to a reference
to access the full paper!

Since flaky tests can pass or fail without any changes to the test code or the
code under test, they are an unreliable indicator of software correctness and a
major problem for many software developers. To address this challenge, my
collaborators and I have developed an automated method that uses machine
learning to predict which tests are most likely to be flaky [@Parry2022a] [{{<
iconify fa6-solid book-open >}}](/research/papers/parry2022a/index.qmd). Along
with proposing a methodology for automatically determining which tests have
latent flakiness [@Parry2020] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open>}}](/research/papers/parry2020/index.qmd), my colleagues and I also
published a survey of the literature relevant to flaky test research
[@Parry2022] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open>}}](/research/papers/parry2022/index.qmd), and a multi-source
investigation into how developers experience the impacts and causes of flaky
tests [@Parry2022b] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open>}}](/research/papers/parry2022b/index.qmd).
Some of my recent work in this area suggests that researchers and developers
should go beyond any individual metric of "good" or "bad" tests --- like test
flakiness --- as it argues for a more holistic view of a test suite's health
[@McMinn2025] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open>}}](/research/papers/mcminn2025/).

My research in this area also shows that flaky test failures often occur in
clusters
whose members share a common root cause, a phenomenon that my collaborators
and I call systemic flakiness, since this result implies that developers can
repair several flaky tests by addressing one underlying problem
[@Parry2025] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/parry2025/index.qmd).
Building on this observation, my colleagues and I revealed that the mutation
operators used to seed synthetic faults can themselves induce flakiness, a
phenomenon that we call test flimsiness and that calls into question any
technique which assumes that a test reacts deterministically to a mutated
program [@Parry2026] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/parry2026/index.qmd).

My collaborators and I have also examined how well detection techniques serve
the developers who repair flaky tests, since automated rerunning detects the
developer-repaired tests in only 40% of the studied commits, which makes it an
unsuitable baseline for judging a technique's usefulness for developers
[@Parry2022c] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/parry2022c/index.qmd). To reduce the cost of
detection without sacrificing its accuracy, my colleagues and I introduced
CANNIER, which combines machine learning models with rerunning-based detection
to decrease the time cost of detection by an order of magnitude
[@Parry2023] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/parry2023/index.qmd). My collaborators and I
have also turned these insights into a practical tool, FlakeFighters, an
extensible PyTest plugin that combines static and execution data to classify a
failing test as a genuine bug or a flaky failure in Python projects
[@Foster2026] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/foster2026/index.qmd).

</div>

Given the importance of verifying that a database application
operates correctly, my PhD dissertation
[@Kapfhammer2007d] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/kapfhammer2007d/index.qmd)
presented and evaluated an approach for testing this type of
software; a notable paper derived from my dissertation is
[@Kapfhammer2003] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/kapfhammer2003/index.qmd).
Since the relational schema preserves the correctness of the database's state,
my research has also focused on testing this complex artifact, with
[@McMinn2015] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/mcminn2015/index.qmd)
and
[@McMinn2019] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/mcminn2019/index.qmd)
being examples of papers.
Recent papers such as
[@Alsharif2020] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/alsharif2020/index.qmd)
and
[@Alsharif2020a] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/alsharif2020a/index.qmd)
present and study techniques for improving the efficiency and effectiveness of
regression testing for relational database schemas by reordering or reducing
the schema's test suites.
To make schema testing practical, my collaborators and I have built tools that
automatically generate test data for integrity constraints, including DOMINO
[@Alsharif2018] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/alsharif2018/index.qmd)
and [@Alsharif2018a] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/alsharif2018a/index.qmd), and SchemaAnalyst,
which supports several test data generators and a reproducible data analysis
workflow
[@Alsharif2018b] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/alsharif2018b/index.qmd)
and [@McMinn2016c] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/mcminn2016c/index.qmd).

This line of work also
includes database-aware coverage monitoring [@Kapfhammer2008] [{{< iconify
fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/kapfhammer2008/index.qmd), search-based
generation of integrity constraint tests [@Kapfhammer2013] [{{< iconify
fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/kapfhammer2013/index.qmd), and the assessment of
the efficiency of that search-based approach [@Kinneer2015] [{{< iconify
fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/kinneer2015/index.qmd). My research has also
built tools that adapted mutation analysis to this domain, enabling the study of
efficient mutation for
database structures [@Wright2013] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/wright2013/index.qmd), the impact of equivalent
and redundant mutants [@Wright2014] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/wright2014/index.qmd), and virtual mutation
analysis [@McMinn2016a] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/mcminn2016a/index.qmd). Complementing these
techniques, my colleagues and I have examined how testers understand SQL test
cases [@Alsharif2019] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/alsharif2019/index.qmd), localized SQL faults
[@Clark2011] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/clark2011/index.qmd), detected dynamic
invariants that a database should satisfy [@Cobb2011] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/cobb2011/index.qmd), and studied the data
stores that such applications rely on [@Arnold2002a] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/arnold2002a/index.qmd).

</div>

In response to the prevalence and complexity of mobile-ready web sites, my
research has developed automated tools for checking the pages in these sites.
Some examples of papers describing methods and prototype tools for automatically
detecting defects
in web pages include [@Walsh2017] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open>}}](/research/papers/walsh2017/index.qmd) and [@Walsh2017a] [{{<
iconify fa6-solid book-open>}}](/research/papers/walsh2017a/index.qmd). Earlier
work in this line detected layout faults that appear
after a developer changes a web page [@Walsh2015] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/walsh2015/index.qmd). The
automated approach introduced in [@Althomali2019] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open>}}](/research/papers/althomali2019/index.qmd) can visually confirm and
classify the reported responsive layout failures in a web page. Building on this
approach, my colleagues and I have also
classified presentation failures that arise from the page's document object
model [@Althomali2021] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/althomali2021/index.qmd). The method
described in [@Walsh2020] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open>}}](/research/papers/walsh2020/index.qmd) can automatically identify
potential regressions from the correct responsive layout of a web page.
Finally, recent work introduced a method that automatically repairs a layout
failure in a responsive web page by effectively "hiding" the defect
from perception
[@Althomali2022] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open>}}](/research/papers/althomali2022/index.qmd).
The experiments in the aforementioned papers study real-world web pages,
ultimately
demonstrating that the presented approaches can automatically detect layout
defects in deployed sites.

Given the challenges associated with accurately judging the quality of a test
suite, my research has designed efficient and useful ways to perform test
assessment through mutation analysis. Presenting and evaluating automated
techniques that efficiently insert synthetic faults into both real-world Java
programs and relational database schemas, some examples of papers include
[@Just2012b] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/just2012b/index.qmd), [@Wright2014] [{{< iconify
fa6-solid book-open >}}](/research/papers/wright2014/index.qmd), and
[@McMinn2019] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/mcminn2019/index.qmd).
Finally, recent work explores how the eXtreme mutation testing (XMT) and
statement deletion (SDL) mutation operators can detect pseudo-tested methods
and statements in a Java program [@Maton2024] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/maton2024/index.qmd).

To bring these techniques into practice, my collaborators and I implemented
PseudoSweep, a tool that automatically identifies pseudo-tested methods and
statements in Java projects by combining method and statement deletion
[@Maton2024a] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/maton2024a/index.qmd). Because developers who
inspect covered but unchecked statements must first choose how to compute the
corresponding oracle gaps, my colleagues and I empirically compared three
calculation approaches and characterized how the discovered gaps differ in
prominence, distribution, and fault detection ability [@Maton2025] [{{<
iconify fa6-solid book-open >}}](/research/papers/maton2025/index.qmd).

My research has also started to use large language models to create mutants,
showing that a hazard-guided approach produces compilable, diverse, and
powerful mutants that reveal defects which prior methods fail to detect
[@Maton2026] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/maton2026/index.qmd). To help other researchers
compare these emerging techniques, my colleagues and I released multiplex, a
modular framework that supports the prototyping and evaluation of
large-language-model-based mutant generation modules across different
languages, models, and build environments [@Maton2026b] [{{<
iconify fa6-solid book-open >}}](/research/papers/maton2026b/index.qmd).

</div>

Since software is often incrementally developed, my research on regression
testing has created research automated ways to efficiently and effectively run
test suites for complex programs. Some examples of papers that present and
evaluate regression testing techniques for reordering and reducing test suites
include [@Walcott2006] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/walcott2006/index.qmd), [@Lin2014] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open
>}}](/research/papers/lin2014/index.qmd), and [@Lin2017] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open
>}}](/research/papers/lin2017/index.qmd). Earlier work in this line developed
knapsack-based and time-aware methods for prioritizing test suites, including
[@Alspaugh2007] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/alspaugh2007/index.qmd), [@Rummel2005a] [{{< iconify
fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/rummel2005a/index.qmd), [@Bhadra2008a] [{{< iconify
fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/bhadra2008a/index.qmd), and [@Kapfhammer2001] [{{< iconify
fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/kapfhammer2001/index.qmd). Papers such as
[@Kapfhammer2007] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/kapfhammer2007/index.qmd), and [@Smith2009a] [{{< iconify
fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/smith2009a/index.qmd) studied how to measure the coverage
effectiveness of a prioritization, [@Williams2010] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open
>}}](/research/papers/williams2010/index.qmd) compared prioritizations with
synthetic test suites, and [@Lin2013] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/lin2013/index.qmd) investigated history-based
prioritization. My research has also reduced the cost of regression testing with
call trees [@Smith2007b] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/smith2007b/index.qmd), cost-aware reduction [@Smith2009]
[{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/smith2009/index.qmd), irreplaceable test cases [@Lin2012]
[{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/lin2012/index.qmd), and methods tailored to database
applications [@Kapfhammer2012a] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/kapfhammer2012a/index.qmd), [@Kapfhammer2007d] [{{<
iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/kapfhammer2007d/index.qmd), [@Alsharif2020] [{{< iconify
fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/alsharif2020/index.qmd), and [@Alsharif2020a] [{{< iconify
fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/alsharif2020a/index.qmd). Complementing these techniques,
my colleagues and I have studied the selection operators used by search-based
prioritization [@Conrad2010a] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/conrad2010a/index.qmd), combined non-redundant mutation
operators with test suite prioritization [@Just2012b] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open
>}}](/research/papers/just2012b/index.qmd), built a framework that supports both
industrial and academic work on these methods [@Kauffman2012a] [{{< iconify
fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/kauffman2012a/index.qmd), and surveyed and empirically
evaluated the field as a whole [@Kapfhammer2010] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open
>}}](/research/papers/kapfhammer2010/index.qmd), [@Kapfhammer2011] [{{< iconify
fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/kapfhammer2011/index.qmd). Leading the way in the
realistic assessment of regression testing methods, papers such as
[@Paterson2018] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/paterson2018/index.qmd) and [@Paterson2019] [{{< iconify
fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/paterson2019/index.qmd), show how to conduct rigorous
regression testing experiments with real program faults. The variance that these
experiments must control when they substitute mutants for real faults also
motivates my recent work on test flimsiness [@Parry2026] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open
>}}](/research/papers/parry2026/index.qmd) which shows that a mutation can
itself make a test outcome non-deterministic.

</div>

Using a fitness function as a guide to a solution,
    search-based methods have shown promise in supporting many software
    engineering tasks. My work has focused on creating frameworks that
support the development of search-based tools, with
[@McMinn2016b] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/mcminn2016b/index.qmd)
being an example.
Other papers like
[@Conrad2010a] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/conrad2010a/index.qmd)
and
[@Kukunas2010a] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/kukunas2010a/index.qmd)
describe search-based solutions to software engineering tasks like regression
testing or
performance optimization. Because the configuration of a search-based generator
strongly influences its results, my colleagues and I have revisited how to tune
the parameters of a generator [@Kotelyanskii2014a] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/kotelyanskii2014a/index.qmd),
compared search-based techniques on synthetic test suites whose properties are
known [@Williams2010] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/williams2010/index.qmd), and applied
search-based
generation to the integrity constraints in relational database schemas with
DOMINO [@Alsharif2018] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/alsharif2018/index.qmd) and SchemaAnalyst
[@McMinn2016c] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/mcminn2016c/index.qmd).
Recent
papers like
[@Alsharif2019] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/alsharif2019/index.qmd)
present experimental methodologies that effectively involve humans when studying
the
usefulness of tests that were generated by search-based techniques.
The search-based automation that these techniques exemplify has more recently
expanded to use large language models in place of a fitness function, as in my
collaborative work on the multiplex framework, which enables the automatic
generation of mutants for a program under test [@Maton2026b] [{{< iconify
fa6-solid book-open >}}](/research/papers/maton2026b/index.qmd).

</div>

Given the importance of equipping software engineers with the
    insights and tools they need to create efficient software, my work has
    developed tools that automatically assess program performance.
Focusing on the empirical evaluation of real-world software components like
databases, relevant papers include
[@Jones2011] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/jones2011/index.qmd),
[@Burdette2012] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/burdette2012/index.qmd),
and
[@Kinneer2015] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/kinneer2015/index.qmd).
Papers such as
[@Kotelyanskii2014a] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/kotelyanskii2014a/index.qmd)
highlight how my research has investigated the influence that the parameters of
a search-based algorithm have on efficiency and effectiveness of methods for
automated test data generation.
My research has also measured the performance of the building blocks that such
systems rely on, including the run-time behaviour of GUI creation frameworks
[@Howell2003a] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/howell2003a/index.qmd), the performance of tuple
space
communication [@Fiedler2005] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/fiedler2005/index.qmd), and the execution of a
test suite inside a resource-constrained environment
[@Kapfhammer2005] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/kapfhammer2005/index.qmd). Since a theoretical
analysis of
an algorithm's worst-case time complexity is difficult to generalize, my
colleagues and I have also inferred that complexity automatically from
empirical measurements [@Kinneer2015a] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/kinneer2015a/index.qmd).

</div>

My surveys of software testing techniques provide a starting
    point for people exploring this field, with
[@Kapfhammer2004] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/kapfhammer2004/index.qmd)
and
[@Kapfhammer2010] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/kapfhammer2010/index.qmd)
being examples of such
articles. Papers like
[@Kapfhammer2016] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/kapfhammer2016/index.qmd)
and
[@McMinn2016] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/mcminn2016/index.qmd)
show how I have articulated a research agenda for the field
of software engineering that stresses, for instance, the need for well-tested
statistical methods. I have also written papers, like
[@Alsharif2018a] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/alsharif2018a/index.qmd)
and
[@Alsharif2018b] [{{< iconify fa6-solid book-open
>}}](/research/papers/alsharif2018b/index.qmd),
that explain how to replicate my empirical studies of search-based testing
techniques.
The statistical rigor and replication practices advocated here also shape my
recent large-scale studies of flaky tests [@Parry2026] [{{< iconify
fa6-solid book-open >}}](/research/papers/parry2026/index.qmd), which analyze
millions of mutant-test pairs collected from over half a million test suite
executions across 28 Python projects.
Because these empirical studies ultimately serve people, my research places a
deliberate emphasis on studies that involve humans, examining how testers
understand SQL test cases [@Alsharif2019] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/alsharif2019/index.qmd),
how developers experience the effects of flaky tests [@Parry2022b] [{{< iconify
fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/parry2022b/index.qmd),
how hybrid methods for reducing schema test suites compare in practice
[@Alsharif2020a] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/alsharif2020a/index.qmd), and how repaired
responsive layouts
are evaluated [@Althomali2022] [{{< iconify fa6-solid
book-open >}}](/research/papers/althomali2022/index.qmd).
